name: porthole
description: Pop the HTML page or Markdown file you are looking at into a floating window: only the rendered page, pinned above your other windows.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Porthole opens local HTML files in VS Code's integrated browser, which reads them from disk.

porthole.sizes.markdownDescription: Size presets for the floating window. A page pops out at the first preset; **Cycle Window Size** steps through the rest. VS Code will not make a window smaller than 400×270.

porthole.position.markdownDescription: Where the floating window opens, in screen pixels, for example `{ "x": 40, "y": 80 }`. Leave as `null` to let VS Code center it on the current window.

porthole.compact.description: Open the floating window in compact mode: no tabs, breadcrumbs or status bar.

porthole.alwaysOnTop.description: Open the floating window pinned above other windows.

enumDescriptions: Show Markdown in Porthole's floating windows with light colors, whatever VS Code's theme.
Show Markdown in Porthole's floating windows with dark colors, whatever VS Code's theme.
porthole.markdown.colorScheme.markdownDescription: Colors of Markdown files shown in Porthole's floating windows. The colors follow the file: while a file is popped out, every preview of it shows these colors; previews of other files keep following VS Code's theme. Code-block syntax colors still follow VS Code's theme.

porthole.outsideLinks.enabled.markdownDescription: Accept `vscode://jlumbroso.porthole/v1/open?file=…` links from outside VS Code, for instance from a terminal, a script or a model. VS Code asks once before it hands Porthole its first link.

porthole.outsideLinks.actions.open.markdownDescription: Let outside links open a page in a floating window.

porthole.outsideLinks.allowWorkspaceFold.markdownDescription: Let outside links open HTML and Markdown files inside the receiving window's workspace folders.

porthole.outsideLinks.allowedFolders.markdownDescription: Further folders, by absolute path, whose HTML and Markdown files outside links may open.

porthole.outsideLinks.allowLocalFiles.markdownDescription: Let outside links open any other local HTML or Markdown file. When off, Porthole asks before opening a file no setting allows.

enumDescriptions: Move it to the main window.
Leave it in the floating window.
porthole.keepToOneTab.markdownDescription: What Porthole does when another extension opens an editor inside one of its floating windows (which brings the tab bar back): move it to the main window, ask, or leave it. A tab with unsaved changes is always left where it is.

porthole.askToKeepCompact.markdownDescription: Ask, at the first pop-out of each session, whether VS Code may lock Porthole's floating windows to one tab (by turning on `workbench.editor.autoLockGroups` for the integrated browser and the Markdown preview). Choosing **Don't Ask Again** sets this to `false`.

porthole.useInternalCommand.markdownDescription: Open the floating window with one internal VS Code command, at the exact preset size. That command is undocumented and may change in any VS Code update; Porthole then falls back on its own. Turn this off to use public commands only: the window opens at VS Code's default size, and size presets do not apply.
